GAMENIGHT / DOCUMENTATION

Phone screens

A game can give every seated player a screen of their own on their phone: a hand of cards, a private vote, a god's view of the map. This is how GameNight does asymmetric play. The TV stays the shared screen; the phone shows what only that player may see. The wire format is in the protocol reference; this page is how to build one.

How it fits together

  1. The game declares a folder with a web page in it.
  2. GameNight serves that page to each signed-in phone at the table, on the LAN or through a hosted room.
  3. The page and the game exchange small JSON messages. GameNight tags every message from a phone with the player who sent it; a phone cannot pretend to be someone else.

The page loads /assets/companion.js, which the host provides:

const game = GameNight.connect((data) => render(data), (status) => showStatus(status));
game.send({ action: "roll" });

In Godot

Keep the page in a folder of your project, such as res://phone, and declare it once from _ready():

func _ready():
    GameNight.companion_presence.connect(_on_phone)
    GameNight.companion_message.connect(_on_phone_message)
    GameNight.declare_companion_folder("res://phone", "index.html")

The host serves pages from a real directory, and an exported game has none: declare_companion_folder copies the folder to user:// and declares that copy. It re-declares after every reconnect. Two export settings decide whether the files are there at all:

  • Add the folder to the export preset's include filter (include_filter="phone/*"), or HTML, JavaScript and CSS files are left out.
  • Set images and fonts in that folder to the Keep File importer (importer="keep" in their .import files). Otherwise Godot exports only its own imported copy and the page loses them. The helper warns about files that were imported instead of kept.

Test the exported game, not only the editor project: these settings only show up there.

GameNight.send_companion_message(data, player_id) reaches one phone, or every phone when player_id is empty. Other engines send the same declare_companion and companion_message messages; see the protocol reference.

In LÖVE

The shared runner declares the page and routes messages when a mode sets phone. A .love file is a zip, so the runner copies the folder to the save directory first and warns when it would not fit a hosted room:

M.phone = {
    folder = "games/cards_phone",
    message = function(state, player, data, send)
        -- a tap from `player`; answer with send(view, player)
    end,
    presence = function(state, player, connected, send)
        if connected then send(view_for(state, player), player) end
    end,
}

Keep the game in charge

The pattern that worked in Hexstead:

  • The game decides, the phone draws. After every change, send each player their whole view: their hand, what they may do now, whose turn it is. The page renders that and sends taps back. Never keep game rules in the page.
  • Send the view again on connect. Phones reload, sleep and reconnect. On companion_presence with connected = true, send that player their current view. Count presence per player: one person can open the page twice.
  • Answer bad moves. Phone messages are untrusted input. Check every action against the rules and send an error back for the page to show.
  • Don't stall the table. A player without their phone open should not block the others. Give them a grace period, then let a bot take the turn.
  • Show the phone player's choices on the TV. Highlight the places or cards the current phone player can pick, so the rest of the table can follow along. Private information stays on the phone; the TV shows shared state.

Fit a hosted room

Hosted rooms forward the page to phones that are not on the PC's network. The bundle must fit:

Limit Value
Files at most 128
Each file at most 512 KiB once base64-encoded (about 384 KB raw)
Whole bundle at most 2 MiB base64-encoded (about 1.5 MB raw)
File types HTML, JavaScript, CSS, JSON, SVG, PNG, JPEG, WebP and WOFF2

Use WOFF2 for fonts, not TTF or OTF, and subset them to the characters you use. Use relative paths only. The page runs in a browser sandbox: no cookies, local storage, external scripts, forms or navigation of the parent app. declare_companion_folder warns when a file or the folder would not fit.

Keep messages under 16 KB. Send the view, not the history.

Native phone apps

When the phone side is a whole game of its own, such as a 3D view, declare a native Android app instead of, or next to, a page:

GameNight.declare_companion(apk_folder, "", {
    "name": "The Voice and the Will",
    "android": "io.ontola.godgame",
    "download": "voice-and-will.apk",
})

The GameNight app installs the APK from the PC and opens it. The app then connects to the game by its own means, for example LAN discovery. Hosted rooms do not relay that connection, so a native app needs the phone on the same network as the PC. Ship the APK inside the game's package next to the executable, and give both the same version, because the game and the app must speak the same protocol. iOS apps are only possible through the App Store.

Two things that bit us: on macOS, binding a socket to * listens on IPv6 only, so bind 0.0.0.0; and a game with mouse capture needs a way to the "join as phone" option from a controller.
